message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), pure water’s freezing (melting) point drops below its normal 0 °C.  
A commonly cited value is about **–2 °C** (roughly –3.6 °F).  

This figure comes from the water‑ice phase diagram; the exact value depends on the purity of the water and the precision of the measurement, but –2 °C is a good approximation for most practical purposes.
